workspace_storage_observation.head_binding_effect: The recorded HEAD identifies workspace context but does not content-bind these untracked files.
workspace_storage_observation.integrity_effect: Their exact physical hashes remain valid candidate facts for this collaborative audit, but neither Git HEAD nor local file mode provides an immutable trust root against a malicious local writer.
workspace_storage_observation.route_consequence: This observation reinforces the explicit accidental-activation threat model and forbids any claim that local hash checks alone resist a hostile local principal.

accepted_r7_completion.effect: The exact post-R7 client and test are accepted only as an offline gate-rebound candidate. Production remains suspended and automatic next permission remains NONE.

authorized_input_pair.hard_rule: The implementer must stop without editing if either input path, byte size, physical SHA-256, workspace, branch, or HEAD differs.

scope_interpretation.current_user_intent: Choose and authorize the smallest fail-closed route that can be implemented and tested offline now, independently reviewed later, and only after a separate final Sol completion permit at most the existing SD0 production preflight and exact seven bounded requests.
scope_interpretation.authorization_now_means: Only the exact current client and test may be modified and tested offline to implement the selected call-layer route. Every production entrypoint must remain suspended until an exact future external Sol completion is explicitly presented at the call boundary.
authorization_now_does_not_mean: permission to make any network request
permission to create a marker, resume file, capability file, or completion file
permission to fetch the ZIP body or any market row
permission to enter D0 or build an adapter, replay, dataset, backtest, paper, testnet, deployment, or trading path
permission to read or use Active G1
permission to install a dependency, provision a key, use Keychain, or create a signing service
scope_interpretation.current_positive_effect: A future implementer may create an offline-only two-file candidate that knows how to authenticate this R8 route, the accepted R7 completion, and a caller-supplied future Sol completion without pinning that future completion digest in source.

trusted_components_and_principals: The exact reviewed Python verifier and interpreter are assumed not to be maliciously rewritten during an activation session.

The external caller who receives the future Sol final report and explicitly supplies completion bytes plus the independently reported physical and canonical digests is a trusted authorization principal.
The operating-system process and exact resolved workspace root are assumed free of hostile debugger, memory-injection, and interpreter-replacement control during the bounded run.
covered_threats: An ordinary caller invokes main, preflight, persist_ready, or execute without an explicit activation capability.
A stale, missing, malformed, duplicate-key, symlinked, nonregular, physically drifted, canonically drifted, wrong-id, wrong-state, or wrong-binding local authority is presented.
A caller accidentally supplies completion bytes without independently supplied expected physical and canonical digests.
A capability is absent, the wrong type, process-stale, root-stale, source-stale, decision-stale, or used outside its exact SD0 permission scope.
An implementer accidentally widens the request allowlist, request order, retry, concurrency, redirects, body caps, output paths, proxy policy, or stage boundary.
A test accidentally reaches a real TCP probe, socket, configured proxy, workspace preflight, workspace runtime, Active G1, market data, or trading action.
explicitly_out_of_scope: A malicious local actor who can modify and execute the Python client or replace the interpreter.
A malicious local actor who can rewrite both local decision files and the code that verifies them.
A caller who intentionally fabricates completion bytes and matching expected digests and then invokes the private capability minting path.
OS-level compromise, debugger or runtime memory injection, monkeypatching in the production process, or hostile dependency replacement.
authoritative_threat_model.why_this_is_the_authoritative_scope: The existing authority chain is unsigned local content-addressed JSON authenticated by hashes embedded in mutable Python source. It provides strong accidental-use and non-adversarial drift closure but no immutable or cryptographic external root that could distinguish a genuine Sol issuer from a malicious actor who controls both local code and local files.
authoritative_threat_model.no_false_security_claim: The selected route is safe only for the covered accidental-activation and non-adversarial-drift model. It is not a security boundary against a hostile local principal with code execution and write access.
authoritative_threat_model.trusted_caller_handoff_semantics: When the same trusted caller supplies both completion bytes and expected digests, the handoff proves explicit caller intent and exact-byte agreement; it does not cryptographically prove that Sol authored the bytes.

if_local_malicious_tampering_becomes_in_.minimum_new_authority_primitive_for_DECI: A stable verification public key anchored outside the writable decision set, a future Sol completion signed by the corresponding externally held private key, and an audited verifier that checks the signature before capability minting.
if_local_malicious_tampering_becomes_in_.additional_primitive_for_CLIENT_TAMPERIN: An externally immutable launcher or verifier, signed immutable client artifact, execution isolation, or equivalent root that the same local actor cannot rewrite.
if_local_malicious_tampering_becomes_in_.key_custody_boundary: Any private signing key must remain external to this repository, client, tests, runtime outputs, Active G1, and this route. This decision does not authorize Keychain integration.

route_options_comparison.name: CALL_LAYER_EXPLICIT_PROCESS_LOCAL_CAPABILITY_PLUS_EXTERNAL_SOL_COMPLETION
route_options_comparison.mechanism: After a future completion exists, a trusted caller explicitly supplies its raw bytes plus independently obtained expected physical and canonical digests. Strict validation mints an opaque process-local, root-bound capability that must be passed as a keyword-only argument to production entrypoints.
route_options_comparison.selection_reason: It creates an explicit, auditable call boundary, preserves default suspension, needs no marker or secret lifecycle, and lets the future completion bind actual post-patch identities without requiring another client edit.

route_options_comparison.name: PREDECLARED_ONE_TIME_CAPABILITY
route_options_comparison.mechanism: Publish or precompute a token now and require it later, optionally attempting to mark it consumed.
route_options_comparison.rejection_reason: A public predeclared token is not a secret, does not prove future Sol completion, and cannot be honestly called one-time across processes without a marker, database, external service, or other durable authority that is outside this task.

route_options_comparison.name: SIGNED_COMPLETION_WITH_KEY_OR_KEYCHAIN_MECHANISM
route_options_comparison.mechanism: Pin a verification key and require a signature over the future completion and post-patch identities.
route_options_comparison.rejection_reason: The authoritative scope is accidental activation and non-adversarial drift, so a signing system has no current net benefit relative to its custody and verifier complexity. No dependency, Keychain integration, or Active G1 coupling is justified. Reconsider only through a new Sol decision if the threat model expands.

entrypoint_policy.main: May accept only an already minted capability as a keyword-only in-process argument; command-line strings, paths, environment values, and flags cannot construct one.
entrypoint_policy.preflight: Requires the exact valid capability before tests evidence, TCP probe, proxy interaction, or output creation.
entrypoint_policy.persist_ready: Requires the same exact valid capability and a ReadyPreflight bound to the same root, authority chain, completion, and source identities before output creation.
entrypoint_policy.execute: Requires the same exact valid capability and ready binding before opener construction or the first logical request.

capability_lifecycle.mint_rule: Within one process, the private registry must reject a second live or previously consumed capability for the same resolved root, R8 identity, completion physical digest, completion canonical digest, and post-patch pair.
capability_lifecycle.preflight_rule: The first preflight atomically changes MINTED to PREFLIGHT_STARTED before the injected or real TCP callback. A non-READY result or exception invalidates the capability; a READY result advances to PREFLIGHT_READY.
capability_lifecycle.persist_rule: persist_ready accepts only the same capability in PREFLIGHT_READY with its exact bound ReadyPreflight and atomically advances to READY_PERSISTED. Any mismatch or failure invalidates it.
capability_lifecycle.execute_rule: execute accepts only READY_PERSISTED, atomically advances to EXECUTION_STARTED before creating runtime outputs or constructing or calling an opener, and advances to CONSUMED_OR_INVALIDATED on every success or failure path.
capability_lifecycle.main_rule: main may inspect but must not advance the capability before delegating to preflight, persist_ready, and optional execute; the delegated entrypoints own the transitions.
capability_lifecycle.reuse_rule: A repeated, reordered, concurrent, or post-failure use of the same capability fails closed before callbacks or new outputs.
capability_lifecycle.cross_process_limit: No global or cross-process one-time guarantee is claimed because no durable consumption authority is authorized.

production_callback_policy.hard_rule: A valid production capability paired with any caller-supplied TCP probe, opener, alternate root, custom proxy, transport, or callback fails closed before the callback is invoked or an output is created.

accepted R7 completion physical and canonical digests
R8 authorization physical and canonical digests
future completion raw-byte snapshot physical and canonical digests
future completion unique activation id and validity window
post-patch client and test physical identities and pair hash

activation_session_binding.stage_revalidation: Before every production-stage transition, re-authenticate the local R7 completion and R8 bytes, recompute client and test identities, revalidate the stored completion snapshot and time window, and compare the exact private registry binding.
activation_session_binding.ready_context_rule: The internal READY context must bind the activation session, completion identities, capability object identity, and generated run_id. No new persisted preflight field is authorized because the frozen measurement contract has an exact field set.
activation_session_binding.decision_or_source_swap_rule: Any authority, completion, client, test, root, READY, run_id, permission, or time-window drift between mint, preflight, persist_ready, and execute invalidates the session before the next callback or output.

selected_activation_route.default_and_failure_behavior: Absent, malformed, forged, copied, stale, wrong-root, wrong-process, wrong-source, wrong-completion, wrong-permission, or already-invalidated capability raises WAIT_DATA_NO_FALLBACK before callbacks, sockets, or outputs.
selected_activation_route.positive_permission_ceiling: After an exact future Sol completion and explicit successful capability minting, at most one bounded SD0 production flow using the frozen preflight and existing seven-request client path is eligible. Existing create-once, stop-on-first-failure, no-overwrite, retry-zero, redirect-zero, concurrency-one, timeout, byte, disk, and cost guards remain mandatory.
selected_activation_route.no_global_one_time_claim: The capability is process-local and must not be described as globally one-time. Cross-process one-time enforcement would require durable external state that this decision does not authorize.

required_one_way_binding_graph: This R8 authorization binds the exact accepted R7 client and test inputs.

The post-patch client hard-pins the externally measured path, physical SHA-256, canonical SHA-256, decision id, and decision state of this already-issued R8 authorization and the already-issued R7 completion.
A future Sol completion binds this R8 authorization and the actual measured post-patch client and test paths, sizes, physical hashes, and pair hash.
The post-patch client does not pin or predict the future completion physical or canonical digest.
At actual invocation, the trusted external caller supplies the exact future completion raw bytes and the physical and canonical digests published by the final Sol review.
The client validates those explicit inputs, its own current identity, the test identity, the R8 chain, and the permission ceiling before minting the in-memory capability.
anti_circular_hash_contract.cycle_absence_explanation: The source hash is an input to the future completion, but the future completion hash is not an input to the source file. The completion is authenticated at the call boundary by externally supplied expected digests, so no post-completion client patch is required.
forbidden_cycle_creators: Adding the future completion digest to client source after final review
Adding a predicted post-patch client or test digest to this R8 decision
Making the completion path or digest discoverable through an environment variable, directory scan, latest-file rule, marker, resume file, or mutable configuration
Treating the completion document's self-reported digest by itself as external authentication
anti_circular_hash_contract.hard_rule: Any implementation that requires changing the client after the future completion binds the post-patch client is outside this authorization and must return to Sol.

external_sol_completion_contract.digest_authority_rule: The expected physical and canonical digests must be explicit values obtained from the future Sol final report by the trusted caller. They must not be read from the completion itself, inferred from a path, discovered dynamically, supplied through the environment, or defaulted.
external_sol_completion_contract.issuer_field_semantics: schema_version, decision_id, issued_by, and issuer-like fields are authenticated content only after the trusted caller supplies the external expected digests. Their names or self-reported values alone are metadata, not cryptographic proof of Sol identity.

required_completion_control_fields.clock_rule: Capability minting requires not_before_utc <= current UTC < expires_at_utc. The remaining lifetime is converted to a process-local monotonic deadline, which every later stage must check.
required_completion_control_fields.replay_scope: The same activation id and completion digest tuple may mint at most one session per process. No cross-process replay claim is made.

required_validation_order: Authenticate the full existing R3-through-R7 chain, the exact accepted R7 completion, and this exact R8 authorization before considering completion bytes.
Require all external call inputs as explicit keyword-only values and reject missing, non-string, non-lowercase-hex, or extra authority inputs.
Hash the raw completion bytes and compare to the externally supplied expected physical SHA-256 before JSON parsing or field reliance.
Parse strict UTF-8 JSON with duplicate-key rejection, finite-number enforcement, exact top-level type, and no trailing or alternate document.
Recompute the domain-separated canonical digest after removing only decision_sha256 and compare it both to decision_sha256 and the externally supplied expected canonical SHA-256.
Authenticate the exact future schema version, decision id, sole accept state, workspace, branch, HEAD, R8 predecessor binding, frozen route, measurement contract, and request plan bindings.
Authenticate the unique activation id, validity-window syntax and ordering, maximum 86400-second window, current UTC eligibility, and process-local monotonic expiry.

Authenticate the future completion's exact post-patch client and test paths, sizes, physical hashes, pair hash, and pair formula against files read without symlink following from the exact resolved root.
Authenticate the required independent implementation review, exact offline test facts, zero-network boundary, output-absence boundary, and permission matrix.

Recompute the current client and test identities immediately before minting and bind them, the root device and inode, process id, R8 identity, completion physical digest, completion canonical digest, and exact permission vector into a private in-process registry entry.

Return only an opaque capability object whose validity is established by object identity plus the private registry entry. Do not return a string, digest, path, boolean, mapping, or serializable token.

The completion file appearing on disk has no automatic effect.
external_sol_completion_contract.completion_rejection_or_absence_effect: All production entrypoints remain WAIT_DATA_NO_FALLBACK before callbacks, sockets, or outputs.

Add keyword-only capability parameters to main, preflight, persist_ready, and execute without accepting strings, paths, mappings, environment values, or CLI flags as capabilities.
Bind every capability to the exact root, root device and inode, process id, current client and test identities, R8 identity, completion identities, and exact SD0 permission vector.

test_changes_allowed: Add only the minimum in-file offline tests required by this decision.

Prove that no synthetic fixture, test callback, patched root, or nonproduction shortcut creates a production-root bypass.

future_sol_final_review_contract.accept_effect: Only the explicit call-layer factory may consider the exact completion raw bytes plus externally published expected digests. No path, file presence, import, test result, or decision issuance automatically resumes production.
future_sol_final_review_contract.reject_or_no_decision_effect: Production remains unconditionally suspended before callbacks, sockets, or outputs.
anti_cycle_final_call_procedure: Sol reviews and hashes the already-finished post-patch client and test.
Sol issues the completion binding those hashes and this R8 authorization.
Sol reports the completion physical and canonical digests externally.

A trusted operator explicitly supplies the completion bytes and those reported digests to the call-layer factory.
Only the returned opaque in-process capability may be passed to the production SD0 entrypoints.

production_permission_ceiling.semantic_boundary: Even a successful seven-request SD0 run can establish only bounded source-document, license, checksum-sidecar, and ZIP-header metadata evidence. It does not establish D0, market-row point-in-time validity, adapter or replay correctness, predictive validity, profitability, deployment readiness, or trading authority.

claim_boundary.maximum_positive_claim: The exact accepted R7 client and test may be modified offline to implement Option A: an explicit standard-library call-layer capability gated by a future external Sol completion. This R8 decision creates no completion or capability, runs no test or network, keeps all production entrypoints suspended, and preserves D0, ZIP GET, market-row, adapter, replay, data, model, paper, deployment, trading, Active G1, credential, order, and funds denial.
